name: Voyager 1
first: Most distant human-made object — currently ~165 AU from the Sun in interstellar space
description: Launched 16 days after Voyager 2, Voyager 1 flew faster and arrived at Jupiter first (1979) and Saturn first (1980). Its Titan flyby bent the trajectory upward out of the ecliptic plane, ending the planetary tour but sending it on the most direct path to the heliopause — which it crossed on 2012-08-25, the first human-made object to enter interstellar space. From a heliocentric distance of ~6 billion km it took the Pale Blue Dot family portrait (1990-02-14), the photograph Carl Sagan wrote about. Both Voyagers carry the Golden Record as humanity’s calling card.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Titan IIIE / Centaur lifts Voyager 1 from Cape Canaveral.

events.label: JUPITER CLOSEST APPROACH
events.note: Flyby at ~349,000 km; discovered Io volcanism, mapped Europa’s surface.

events.label: SATURN + TITAN FLYBYS
events.note: Titan flyby bent trajectory out of the ecliptic plane — no further planetary encounter possible.
